LESSON: CHEMICAL BONDING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Matter and Chemical Reactions
Topic 2.3: Chemical bonding
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Chemical bonding, part of Matter and Chemical Reactions in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How do bond types relate to physical properties of compounds?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Chemical bonding together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: as the learner sensitises the community on use and care of common appliances such as

utensils and other cookware.

● Digital literacy: as the learner navigates through online sources with assistive technology to access virtual laboratories for

simulations on formation of chemical bonds.

● Creativity and imagination: as the learner undertakes a project of modelling ball and stick ionic and covalent structures

of selected molecules using locally available resources.

Values:
● Respect: as the learner recognises and appreciates the input of every group member when discussing the relationship

between bond types and physical properties of different structures.

● Patriotism: as the learner sensitises the community on use and care of common appliances such as utensils and other

cookware.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Socio Economic and environmental issues -Safety and Security: as the learner observes safety precautions when carrying

out activities to investigate properties of elements and compounds.

● Socio Economic and environmental issues - Financial Literacy: as the learner makes informed decisions when selecting

appropriate items, appliances and equipment made from specific elements and compounds.
